detail: We buy '1 stick, finely chopped (120 g)' but no step uses celery; the source (natashaskitchen) sautes it with the onion and carrot in step 2.
We buy 1 tbsp Worcestershire but no step uses it; the source stirs it in with the tomatoes and broth in step 3.
We buy 1/4 tsp sugar but no step uses it; the source seasons the vegetables with sugar in step 2.
We buy 1 tbsp olive oil but the steps brown the beef with no oil mentioned; the source browns the beef in oil in step 1.
We buy 2 tsp salt but the steps never say salt or season; the source seasons in step 2.
We buy 1/2 tsp pepper but the steps never say pepper or season.

Our title promises 'Cilantro Lime Rice' and the source's rice uses lime zest/juice and 1 cup cilantro, but our list and steps contain no cilantro or lime; our rice step substitutes 'a squeeze of the pineapple juice'.
We buy 18.75 tbsp fresh mint but no step uses mint; the filling step instead says to stir in 'chopped fresh basil' (the source kibbeh uses mint/basil in the shell mixture).
Step 5 says 'stir in the chopped fresh basil off the heat' but basil is not in our list; the purchased herb is fresh mint, so the step names the wrong herb.
We buy 0.5 tbsp garlic powder but no step uses it; the source (realfoodwholelife) includes it in the beef seasonings in step 3.
We buy 4.25 cups dry rice for 'Rice Bowls' but no step ever cooks or combines the rice; the steps end at shredding the beef into the consomme.

The source braises in 750ml Pinot Noir, the ingredient the dish is named for; our card replaces it with beef broth only, with no acid (vinegar/grape juice) substituted - likely the deliberate site-wide no-alcohol adaptation, but nothing replaces the wine's role.
We buy 2 tsp olive oil but no step uses it; the source heats the oil before browning the beef.
We buy salt 'to taste (15 g)' but the steps never say salt or season; the source seasons in step 2.
We buy pepper 'to taste (4 g)' but the steps never say pepper or season.
